name: Arcturus PD-6 'Peacemaker'
description:
A compact .45 ACP semi-automatic pistol marketed for civilian self-defense, representing the opposite philosophy of the Citizen's minimalism. The Peacemaker is overbuilt — a stainless steel frame, match-grade barrel, tritium night sights, and a 10-round magazine of hollow-point .45 ACP that will stop anything short of armored cyberware. Arcturus designed it for civilians who want the same stopping power as professional operators, packaged in a weapon that fits in a belt holster.

The Peacemaker is controversial because it represents deliberate escalation of civilian armament. The .45 ACP hollow-point round is a manstopper — designed to expand on impact, create maximum tissue destruction, and transfer all kinetic energy to the target. This is not a deterrent. It is a killing tool marketed to people who park in office garages and buy groceries on their way home. Arcturus's marketing — 'When Peace Requires Authority' — positions the weapon as a civic responsibility, as if carrying a .45 designed for maximum lethality is an act of community service.

The PD-6 has become the weapon of choice for civilian gun enthusiasts in GLMZ who view self-defense as an identity rather than a contingency. These owners train, practice, accessorize, and carry daily with a commitment that approaches religious devotion. The weapon has spawned a subculture of civilian operators who dress, train, and equip themselves like professional security without the license, experience, or accountability. Arcturus encourages this subculture because it sells weapons, accessories, training courses, and the lifestyle that goes with them.
legality: Licensed — civilian self-defense permit with enhanced caliber authorization
specifications:
caliber: .45 ACP
action: Semi-automatic, single-action
magazine: 10 rounds
effective range: 25 meters
weight: 0.9 kg
length: 205mm
sights: Tritium night sights
finish: Stainless steel, brushed
tactical_use: Personal defense with maximum stopping power. The Peacemaker is designed to end threats with minimal rounds fired — the .45 ACP hollow-point creates wound channels that incapacitate faster than smaller calibers. The match-grade barrel provides accuracy that exceeds most civilian shooters' capability.
cultural_context: The Peacemaker has become a cultural marker in GLMZ — carrying one signals a specific identity: someone who takes self-defense seriously enough to carry a .45, trains regularly, and has adopted the mindset that they might need to kill someone today. The weapon has created a civilian operator subculture that mimics military culture without military accountability.
known_users: Small business owners in high-threat areas
story_hooks: A Peacemaker owner shot and killed a teenager who was reaching for a BCI display pad that the shooter mistook for a weapon. The legal defense is citing Arcturus's training program, which teaches civilians to 'treat every potential threat as a confirmed threat.' Arcturus's marketing created the mindset that killed the teenager.

Arcturus has discovered that a competitor is selling counterfeit Peacemakers with inferior metallurgy — the weapons fire normally for 200 rounds, then the barrel fails catastrophically. Thirty thousand counterfeit units are in civilian hands, and there's no way to identify them without firing them.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, purposeful semi-automatic pistol with classical lines and a boxy, utilitarian silhouette. The Peacemaker projects understated lethality—no flash, no tactical rail clutter, just efficient geometry. The proportions suggest serious intent: a squared-off grip, clean slide, and the visual weight of stainless steel.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 205mm | Height: 140mm | Grip width: 32mm | Barrel length: 127mm
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and balanced. At 0.9kg, it sits heavy in the hand with reassuring heft—dense stainless steel that conveys manufacturing precision rather than ergonomic compromise.
physical_description.primary_material: Stainless steel frame and slide; match-grade barrel; polymer grip panels
physical_description.finish: Brushed stainless steel with a matte, non-reflective surface. The finish shows controlled tool marks and deliberate hand-finished characteristics. No aggressive polishing—the steel has a businesslike, industrial sheen.
physical_description.color_scheme: Stainless steel gray with charcoal polymer grip inserts. Tritium night sight posts glow faintly green. No decorative elements or anodizing.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer panels with subtle checkering—engineered for wet conditions and gloved hands. The backstrap is contoured; the frontstrap features aggressive diagonal grooves. Bare stainless trigger and safety lever.
distinctive_features: Fixed tritium night sights with glowing green front and rear posts—visible in darkness without electronics
Match-grade barrel visible at the muzzle with precision-machined crown
Single-action trigger with audible, positive reset
Beaver-tail grip safety that requires conscious full grip to disengage
Ten-round magazine with witness holes and aggressive witness grooves
Minimalist slide serrations (rear only) for manipulation without flashiness
Rounded edges and corners—no sharp snags, pure functional design
Magazine release button integrated cleanly into frame without protrusions
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Iron Point Ammunition logo (stylized compass point) engraved on left slide. 'Arcturus PD-6' stamped along right slide. 'PEACEMAKER' in sans-serif block letters across the slide. Serial number on right frame. '.45 ACP' caliber stamp on barrel visible at breech.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained and meticulously clean. Civilian operators keep the Peacemaker in pristine condition—it's a status object as much as a tool. The stainless finish shows minimal wear unless actively carried daily, in which case it may show light holster wear on the rear sight and muzzle.
